FLOWVIEW FIELD GUIDE

Make the system make sense.

A practical guide to building diagrams people can follow.

START HERE01 · Your first diagram02 · Find your way BUILD THE STORY03 · Nodes & connections04 · Steps & playback05 · Alternate outcomes06 · Visual panels07 · A story at home08 · Layouts & audiences CONNECT & SHARE09 · Services & evidence10 · Copy & reuse11 · Save & share12 · Work with an agent13 · When something surprises you

01 / YOUR FIRST DIAGRAM

Start with a small, complete story.

Flowview combines a system diagram with a sequence of events. The diagram shows who is involved; steps show what happens; panels show what changes for people and devices.

  1. Open a useful starting point. On the home page choose Start new project → Simple service flow. Or choose Blank diagram if you want to start empty.
  2. Make the actors yours. Click a node in the preview. In Inspect, change its title and sub (the one-line detail). Press Enter or leave the field to apply it.
  3. Add something. Choose Add to diagram → Node, then click a preset to add it. The Into selector chooses the destination section.
  4. Connect the actors. Alt/Option-click the source node, release the key, then click the destination. Give the new connection a meaningful label, such as “Request recording.”
  5. Walk through it. Open Steps. Select a step, then Inspect selected step to edit its caption. Add another with Append step. Use ADD TO STEP to choose the nodes and connections active at that moment, then finish the mode.
  6. Keep a copy. Choose save in the editor’s file controls to save the editable JSON. Use export… when you want a viewable HTML page too.
Build one happy path first. Get the starting event, meaningful changes, and outcome right. Then add failure paths and a second view for another audience.

02 / FIND YOUR WAY

Preview on one side. The selected thing on the other.

Click a node, connection, panel, or step to inspect it. Inspect edits the selection, Steps manages the story, and JSON exposes the complete source. You can do ordinary editing without writing JSON. If you do edit JSON, choose Render and read any validation messages.

Page
The whole document, with one or more sections and optional tabs.
Section
One diagram, its panels, and its timeline.
Node / connection
An actor and a directed communication between actors.
Step / path
A moment in the story and the sequence of moments for an outcome.
View
An arrangement of the same section for an audience. It can show fewer panels and fewer stops.

The left rail opens Inspect, Steps, Outline, JSON, or File beside it. Each fills the editor; the preview stays on the right. Drag the visible divider right for more editing room. File → Workspace preferences contains Focus workspace and Reset editor width. The top toolbar keeps Add to diagram, Undo, Redo, User guide, and Save available. Use Outline (⌘/Ctrl K) to find objects across sections and tabs. Canvas selection updates Inspect without switching away from another tool.

The Flowview wordmark and ← New / open return home. Browser Back and Forward work between entry screens and the editor. Continue brings back your current project.

03 / NODES & CONNECTIONS

Arrange the actors. Make each connection explain itself.

Rows keep nodes ordered left to right. Drag a node to another row or position to reorganize the flow. For arbitrary placement, select the node and choose float → Free placement, then drag it anywhere or adjust Float X / Y. Choose an automatic float position or return it to rows when you want automatic placement again.

Edge routing belongs to the whole diagram. Select its section heading or Outline entry, then choose Inspect → Edge routing → No lanes (default) or Lanes. New projects, built-in templates, catalog seeds and trace imports start without lanes. Opening an existing spec preserves its setting. Lanes reserve connector tracks between rows and require 1–5 unstacked nodes per row, no floats or self-loops; other layouts use curves. This is separate from the story lane labels on steps.

To draw a connection, Alt/Option-click a source, then click a destination. You can also use Connect from this node in the inspector, or Add to diagram → Connection. A preview arrow shows where you are connecting. Esc cancels. Connections stay within a section; an existing ordinary connection is not duplicated.

Select the connection to edit its label, Connection type, and arrow behavior. All built-in protocols are available. Use New connection type… for a custom name/color; creation also assigns it to this connection. Edit connection type updates its name/color everywhere in the document. Step inspectors provide the matching Story lane and New lane… controls. Display-name edits preserve IDs and advanced palette colors; setting a color replaces that palette. Exit side and Entry side choose its attachment edges; the position percentage moves an endpoint along that side. Use these when automatic routing obscures a relationship.

Click any bullet or subpoint to edit it directly. Add sibling and Add subpoint grow the list; Indent, Outdent, and Move point up/down move the whole subtree in one undoable edit. The Outline includes every nested point. Prose textareas offer Bold, Italic, Code, Code block, and a URL field with Insert link. Select text before formatting. Enter and Tab keep their normal text-editing behavior.

Connections, bullets, and contract fields have Visibility by path position in their inspector. Choose Show from position and Hide starting at position, using the full story’s captions as a guide. These one-based positions apply on every alternate path, even if a view hides some stops; they stay in place when you reorder steps. Caption path previews the other path’s captions. The current-position buttons use the full path position. Ambient mode shows everything.

Fit width uses the available width; Readable preserves node readability and lets you pan horizontally when the board overflows. These controls change your viewing scale, not the authored node positions.

Give a large process its own detail. A node’s Create detail flow starts a drilldown into another section. Readers keep context through the overview map and breadcrumbs. In Domain detail, apply a local child section, then map When parent event to a Child path and Child event. Valid row edits save directly; Preview mapping opens the saved child position, even when that view normally hides the stop. Unset choices inherit the detail entry defaults. Imported numeric positions and advanced fields stay intact; Advanced mapping JSON remains available. Apply changed entry defaults before editing mappings. Choosing another child section or target type resets its entry position, mappings, and boundary ports; unrelated metadata is retained. A pointer to another diagram is a separate document handoff, useful for an independently maintained process.

04 / STEPS & PLAYBACK

A step is a change, not a screenshot.

Use Steps to select, search, append, duplicate, or move beats earlier and later. A useful caption explains what changed and why: “The recording service stores the clip before notifying the resident.” Captions and prose support backticks for inline code and triple backticks for code blocks; node labels stay plain text.

ADD TO STEP selects the nodes, edges, and panels involved in a beat. Finish this mode before trying to edit or connect objects normally. Panel fields describe what changes at that beat. A value you do not change usually carries forward from earlier steps on the selected path. The Effective state · all panels inspector explains whether a value is initial, set here, inherited, or transient.

Use the numbered circles and previous/next controls to walk the story. Play starts automatic advancement; Pause holds the current beat. Under Playback settings, choose the opening view and whether it should autoplay. The editor starts paused even when the exported viewer is configured to autoplay. Ambient view animates the overall diagram; step view follows one path.

You can color an individual step circle to mark a phase change without making an alternate path. Use a branch only when the outcome or sequence actually differs.

Story time. When the story happens at a particular time, first decide its span: when it starts and when it ends. Select the section and open Story time and device defaults. Enter a Start such as 2026-09-24T22:30, optionally an End, and choose the Clock (12-hour or 24-hour) and Date format. Then select a step and set its Story time: +45m moves forward from the previous step, 06:50 jumps to the next 6:50, and a full date-time sets it exactly. Leave it empty to keep the previous step’s time. The note underneath shows the resolved time on the selected path. Phone, Device app and App screens clocks and dates follow the step automatically; a clock or date you type on a panel still wins at that step until the story time next moves. Clear Start to turn story time off.

Batteries drain with the elapsed story time and charge while their trend is charging. Ask the device owner or check the source for the real rates, then set diagram-wide Drain %/h and Charge %/h under the same section group, or override them on a Battery panel. Empty rate fields show the built-in default (placeholder): it keeps a sketch moving but is not a fact about your device. If you keep it, say on the page that the battery is an illustrative estimate. New battery panels start with the diagram’s rates. In a step’s battery changes, Extra drain % subtracts a one-time cost such as a recorded clip, and charge sets a known reading from which the drain continues. Effective state labels these values Story time or Story time · battery drift, adding built-in default rate when a placeholder rate is in use. Device app battery cards show what the app last received; set them at the step the report arrives.

Report times. Don’t type “Updated just now” or “Updated 3 h ago” into a Device app card: it will be wrong a few steps later. Instead, on the step where the app receives new data, open that card under Panel changes, set its value and press Reported at this step (in Starting state the button reads Reported at story start). On every later step the card works out its own text from the story time: Updated just now, Updated 5 min ago, Updated 3 h ago, and Last report with the date and time after a day. The Report time box also takes -15m (15 minutes before this step), 06:05 (the latest 6:05 at or before this step) or a full date-time. Clear report time stops the computed text from this step on, even when the report came from an earlier step; Inherit removes this step’s report time so the earlier report applies again. In the panel’s fields table, set a card’s freshness to absolute to show “Last report 6:05 PM” instead, or off to keep your own text. Text you type in detail still wins until the next report. Freshness never marks a card Cached; choose that status yourself. Effective state labels the computed text Story time · derived freshness. Without a story start, report times are ignored.

05 / ALTERNATE OUTCOMES

Show where the same story goes differently.

An alternate belongs on the same diagram: a dropped signal, a retry, a rejected request, or a recovery. Keep the common lead-in shared, then show the first different event.

Happy path1234
Recovery1234
Shared ending5

Shared beginning → independent outcome → one shared ending

  1. Select the last shared step in the Steps tab. If the first different event is step 3, select step 2.
  2. Choose + Alternate after selected step. The first branch creates a happy path and an orange alternate. Rename the alternate to its outcome and set its color with Update path.
  3. Edit the new independent step, then append what happens next. An alternate can end early; it does not need as many steps as the happy path.
  4. To rejoin downstream processing, use Reuse steps… → Use shared steps for the common operations. They appear once on a common track, with connecting lines showing the join. Add independent events afterward to split again, and share later events to rejoin. A shared ending means every participating path finishes there. Use Copy and customize when events should evolve separately.
Shared means one editable event. Editing a shared step changes it in every path that uses it. Choose Make independent here before making a path-specific change. A common track shows shared downstream operations. Shared beginnings can appear as faded circles. A matching caption alone does not make two steps shared.

Clicking a path chip starts at step 1, including its shared lead-in. Clicking a shared circle keeps the selected path if it participates; otherwise the circle identifies the path it will select. Its numbers and state follow that path. A retry flag or earlier log entry carries through shared operations unless a step changes it. An early-ending path never joins a later block it does not visit. Hiding stops in a view does not change the authored joins or endings. Represent a communication that fails with Add failed communication on that step; make the edge visibly break and explain the consequence. Do not animate a successful delivery that never happened.

Remove from this path only removes membership. Delete from all paths removes the event everywhere. Read the affected paths before deleting a shared step.

06 / VISUAL PANELS

Show the consequence outside the arrows.

Choose Add to diagram → Panel. The large picker shows a preview and description; select one, then explicitly add it. Pick panels that answer a question, rather than filling every slot.

  • Home shows people, rooms, cameras, doors, and physical activity.
  • Screen and device app show video clips, notifications, battery or camera data. Resize its layout tile to scale the phone, text, and cards together. Device app stays in a phone frame: choose its Starting phone screen, then use each step’s Phone screen control to move between Home screen and Device app. Under Starting state, set each card’s value, status, detail, and Card visibility. Hide cards that appear later. Each step’s Card visibility control shows or hides a card while keeping its data. Use Notifications → Add notification to write its App, Title, and Message. Reorder or remove cards in the composer; its preview shows your text. Clear earlier notifications clears the old stack before adding this step’s cards. Starting state supports the same composer for Phone and Device app. Notifications and card values carry independently of screen changes. Data sources are optional; add them when explaining where a value comes from.
  • Monitoring and dispatch connect an operator’s video review to an emergency response.
  • Software and telemetry panels make queues, database delays, logs, gauges, and other state visible. Browse the picker for the available types.

Choose Browse icons beside an icon field to see colored choices, search names, or filter by category. This works for nodes, groups, Home elements and Device app cards. In Device app, set a card’s default under fields → icon; use its Starting state → icon or a selected step’s Panel changes → card → icon to show a different state such as charging. Icon choices carry independently of values and freshness. Inherit removes the selected step’s assignment and uses the earlier path state.

To reuse a company name and logo, select a Phone, Device app, Camera screen or Security monitoring panel and expand Company branding. Choose Shared across this diagram to edit every inheriting panel at once, Override for this panel for a local variation, or No brand on this panel. Enter Company / app name and choose a Library icon, a short Monogram, or Upload logo. Uploads accept PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 512 KiB and 4096 × 4096 pixels. Logos travel with the saved file. A local mark replaces the shared mark.

Select a Camera or Device app panel and open Starting state to set its initial mode or values using the same controls as a step. These values begin every path; edits here preserve step overrides. Unset fields use panel defaults. Set the panel’s starting values, then change only what matters in each step. Recording and scene activity are separate: a camera can start recording before a person enters the scene. A panel with no changes in the current step can still show state inherited from earlier beats.

To hide an entire panel until it matters, select it and set Starting visibility to Hidden until a step shows it. Then select a step in the Steps tab, open Inspect, and use Panel changes → Panel visibility. Every panel has Show, Hide, and Inherit. Show and Hide carry forward on that path; Inherit removes this step’s override. Hidden panels keep their space and continue receiving updates. Attached playback controls stay usable. Use Outline to select a hidden panel. Layout-hidden elements stay hidden; Ambient shows all panels included in the view.

Camera step fields and Phone audio have a duration selector. Enter a value, then choose Carry forward or This step only. Inherit previous state removes this step’s assignment. Audio changes replace the whole audio snapshot, rather than inheriting individual audio fields. If an imported patch has both a temporary and carried value, ordinary edits affect the temporary value and preserve what resumes afterwards; explicitly choosing a duration keeps the temporary value and replaces the pair. Starting state and notifications have their own behavior.

07 / A STORY AT HOME

Place the house once. Animate what happens there.

Start with A connected home to see rooms, actors, devices, and an outage together. Choose Edit layout on the Home panel to edit its shared house, rooms, devices, doors, and subjects. Expand an element’s collapsed inspector group to see its fields.

In Edit layout, expand a device or subject row and use icon → Browse icons to choose its marker. Cameras and hubs keep their normal behavior when you change their icon. Leave the choice empty to keep the normal camera, router, sensor or person marker.

In shared layout mode, drag devices, doors, and people; use a room’s border or label to move it. The house grip moves its outline, and corner handles resize the house or rooms. Moving a room or the house outline does not move its contents. Outdoor areas can sit around the house or beside an indoor room.

For a marker that changes during the story, use Starting device and subject conditions for its initial icon, or the selected step’s Home at this step → element → icon. Choose Inherit previous icon to follow the earlier state, Restore layout icon to reset its marker, or Browse icons for a new choice. Icon changes preserve the device’s state and the subject’s position; show a hidden subject before changing its icon on that step.

Choose Edit home at current step to animate an event. This edits that moment instead of the shared floor plan. Use Inherit to remove an override and take the earlier path value. A device’s temperature and operating state are separate, so an overheated camera can remain visibly hot after shutting down.

Doors pivot at their hinge: width sets the leaf’s length, facing sets the closed direction, and swing sets its opening angle. Change the door’s state at the relevant step. Subject labels are off by default; enable them when names help. A cloud belongs under devices using the cloud icon; subjects are moving actors.

Keep time honest. “Recording begins,” “visitor walks away,” and “resident receives the clip” are often different steps. Give each its own visible change.

08 / LAYOUTS & AUDIENCES

One story. More than one useful view.

Choose Arrange section to position and resize the diagram, panels, and step controls. Use View name for reader-facing names such as “At home” and “Service flow.” Duplicate a view, then tailor it for another audience.

Choose Presentation → Standard for your authored arrangement or Explore for a full-height graph with independent floating panels and pinned step controls. In Explore, drag a panel header, resize its corner or hide it while inspecting the story. Panels chooses available panels; Hide panels / Restore panels clears or restores them, and Stack at edge returns them to the right side. Expand gives the graph more room. Reader changes do not rewrite your diagram. In the workbench, panel and step-control positions and sizes, plus diagram pan and zoom, save to this view automatically. Each gesture is one Undo action; Escape cancels a drag. Use the small grip on the step bar to move it and its corner to resize it. Drag empty graph space to pan a quarter-screen past each edge. Keep Standard as the default business view and use Explore for an engineering view. Presentation belongs to the named view across all host previews, and duplicating a view keeps it. Changing Presentation is one Undo/Redo operation. Explore stays visible while arranging. Optimize layout or Reset layout restores its automatic edge stack and diagram sizing while keeping hidden panels hidden. Saved defaults scale to the viewer’s available space.

Under Visible elements, each panel and the data diagram has its own checkbox for the selected layout. Hide Home in the engineering view or hide Data flow in the customer view. Optimize layout arranges the visible elements and respects the hidden set. Make default chooses the opening view. Property edits, Undo/Redo, and host preview changes keep your current view selected. Opening another project uses its own default; deleting the selected view falls back to the remaining default. Done arranging returns to ordinary use.

Attach the step controls to Home or Data flow to keep them in the same outlined frame, or detach them for independent placement. Resize attached controls with their height adjustment. Under Steps shown in this view, select only the stops that audience needs. Skipped steps still happen: their effects carry forward. This shortens the presentation, not the story.

Preview Responsive, Backstage, or Confluence to tune space for the destination. These are layout previews, not live connections to those products. Named views are the complete set of view buttons; create a view named “Data flow” if you want one alongside your other arrangements.

09 / SERVICES & EVIDENCE

Make the picture traceable.

Canon diagrams on the home page opens the published library read-only. You can play steps, switch paths and views, and follow evidence links. A guided tour offers a walkthrough on your first visit; choose the ? button to replay it. Skip or finish the tour to return to reading. On later diagrams, New features to explore offers just the tour topics you have not seen, for your chosen walkthrough. This learning history stays in your browser. Copy link shares a direct read-only URL to a published diagram, even before Backstage is connected. You can also open a library card in a new tab. Edit in Workbench opens a local editable copy. It does not overwrite or approve the canonical source; save your changes and submit them through your team’s repository process. Keep maintained JSON specs and generated HTML together under diagrams/<name>/. After review, add the folder and its owner to root canon.json. The normal build publishes that list for the workbench; Backstage uses the same membership. Per-spec flags do not enroll a diagram. Saving an editor draft does not change canon membership.

To seed a graph, choose From service catalog on the home page or Add to diagram → Services from catalog. Pick the services you need. Optional connections come from declared dependencies and API relationships. A single connection lists all consumed APIs for that service pair, along with any explicit dependency. Existing connection labels stay as authored. These connections do not establish the runtime ordering of your feature.

On a node, choose Company service, then Service API and API operation where available. Selecting a service fills an empty name but preserves an authored one. The hosted editor loads its bundled catalog automatically. For a manual snapshot, choose File → Company repository, paste catalog JSON, and choose Load catalog.

Code references are a separate authoring task. Use Code and trace evidence on a step to reference the repository, file, and reviewed revision. Viewers can follow those links. A code change is drift evidence, not proof that behavior changed; a person reviews that decision.

For a trace-based starting point, choose File → Import and use the trace importer with pasted or exported trace JSON. Check the observed services and timings before treating it as the intended design. A missing span alone does not prove a failed communication.

10 / COPY & REUSE

Choose whether the relationship should stay shared.

Use Copy, Paste…, and Duplicate for selected nodes, panels, or sections. Multi-select nodes to copy a group; internal connections travel with them when both endpoints are included. A copied section includes its story and alternate paths. A copied panel carries its layout and starting state, not the current step’s animation.

In Home’s shared layout inspector, use Copy element or Duplicate element for its contents. For story events, use Reuse steps…: copying creates an independent event, while sharing deliberately keeps one event on multiple paths. Consecutive shared events can form a common middle block or ending. Check Destination preview to see the state they receive from this path’s earlier steps. Undo reverses an operation as a unit.

⌘/Ctrl C, ⌘/Ctrl V, and ⌘/Ctrl D operate on diagram objects outside text fields. Inside a text field, normal text editing takes priority. If clipboard permission is unavailable, Paste… provides a manual text option.

11 / SAVE & SHARE

Keep the source. Share the experience.

save
Keep the editable JSON. Open it later to continue authoring.
export…
Write the JSON and a standalone viewer HTML page to a folder. Share or host the HTML for readers.
Export for Confluence
Download the payload for the Flowview Forge integration.
Copy JSON for Confluence
Copy that payload to paste into the integration’s configuration.
Copy link / Copy embed link
Link to a viewer’s selected section, view, path, and step. Share a hosted viewer URL your readers can reach.

The browser draft is convenient recovery, not a repository commit or a backup. Save JSON before clearing browser data or moving computers. Confluence and Backstage publication depend on your company’s integration and access controls; exporting or editing here does not publish to either one.

12 / WORK WITH AN AGENT

Give it the question, the evidence, and the audience.

On the home page choose Build it with your agent. Select whether to explain a design, explore a codebase, or improve a diagram. Add your brief, choose the audience, and copy the prompt. It points your agent to the authoring skill in the selected repository. Use Using a company fork? to set your team’s repository and revision.

Who is it for? also sets the technical level. Business readers get a story-level diagram: people, devices, app screens and outcomes, with the backend as a few named boxes, and the agent asks no technical questions; it lists the technical choices it made in the ledger under “Decisions I made” for an engineer to review. Engineers get every service hop, API and code reference. For a new diagram or a changed story, expect one short batch of plain questions first (at most seven) about whatever your brief leaves open: takeaway, the moments to show, time span, outcomes and starting state. Answer them; the story depends on them. Its storyboard worksheet is in the coverage ledger. Review it before the JSON: clocks, battery and other values should change as time passes, every step should light each connection it uses, and icons should match state.

Explain what happens from a doorbell press to a resident seeing the clip. Include the successful path, a recording timeout with recovery, and an outage that ends early. Give engineers a service view and business readers a Home view of the same steps. Use the attached design as evidence; identify anything it does not establish.

Run the agent in your own tools with the relevant design or code. Bring its JSON back using Paste JSON or Open file, then walk every path. For a local session, run node tools/agent-session.mjs in the built Flowview checkout and open the printed URL. Give the agent the scratch folder’s README. Your selections and source flow into local files; agent proposals apply automatically as one Undo action. Finish typing or dragging and click the canvas to let a waiting update apply. Use Agent files · Disconnect to stop sharing; File → Local agent session shows the folder and status. Ask it to check readability, animation, failure consequences, and shared-step behavior as well as JSON validity.

13 / WHEN SOMETHING SURPRISES YOU

Usually, it is the editing context.

“Editing the alternate changed the happy path.”
That event is shared. Use Make independent here before changing its content for one path.
“My new branch starts with the same event.”
Create it after the last shared step. The next step is the first independent outcome. The shared lead-in still plays from step 1.
“The camera is still recording on this step.”
State carries forward. Set recording off at the appropriate beat; changing a scene does not automatically end recording.
“I hid a step, but its result is still visible.”
A view skips presentation stops, not their effects. Use an alternate path to change what actually happens.
“I can’t move the house or edit its rooms.”
Choose Edit shared home layout; step editing changes the event rather than the floor plan.
“Clicks keep highlighting things instead of editing them.”
Finish ADD TO STEP or cancel a pending connection with Esc.
“The service dropdown is empty.”
The catalog has not loaded or has no matching services. Check File → Company repository for its status, then import a snapshot if needed.
“The editor or diagram feels squeezed.”
Drag the workspace divider, or choose File → Workspace preferences → Focus workspace. Try Readable size for a wide graph, and arrange the section for the target host.

Start small. Walk every outcome. Let every animation explain a change.

Playback settings

Applies to this section and all its paths when entering step view. Off by default; plays every 3 seconds when on. The editor preview always starts paused.

Select a beat to edit it or branch after it. Step content is shared by paths that reference it. Append, duplicate and move affect the selected path; deleting a step removes it everywhere. Copies repeat patches, including appended events. Reveal/hide indices stay positional within each path.

Honeycomb trace → diagram

Paste event JSON or open an export, preview its size, then choose all exported spans or a focused branch. Conversion runs locally. Build diagram replaces the editor in one undo step.

Custom field names

Default fields: trace.trace_id, trace.span_id, trace.parent_id, service.name, name, timestamp, duration_ms, error. Override only the fields that differ. Time is ISO with timezone or Unix seconds; duration is milliseconds.

Focus keeps exported descendants so included spans retain child timing. Parent IDs at the boundary remain unchanged.

      page{title, skin?, protocols?, lanes?, blocks}The whole doc page. skin: aurora daylight editorial terminal pastel blueprint (pastel default). sections is accepted as an alias for a blocks list with no tabs.
      
      
      page.blocks[n]section | {tabs:[...]}Ordered content. A block is either a section object (below) or a tabs container.
      
      
      tabs[n]{label, sections:[...]}One tab: a label and its sections. All tabs render; inactive panels are hidden (their ambient animation stops painting). Arrow keys move between tabs.
      
      
      page.protocols{kind: {label, color}}Extends the built-in kind table (https, int, mqtt). color is one hex, or {aurora, daylight}. Edges, packets, arrowheads, and the legend all read this one table, so they cannot drift.
      
      
      page.lanes{LANE: {color, label?}}Declares step lanes (e.g. NET / DEV / CAM). A step tagged lane shows a colored pill on its caption line.
      
      
      sections[n]{heading?, accent?, source?, text?, bullets?, contract?, diagram?}One bounding box. accent: green blue violet amber pink cyan red slate or a hex; defaults cycle. text is a paragraph or list of paragraphs. source: optional permalink (HLD section) — renders a small "source↗" chip beside the heading, new tab.
      
      
      sections[n].contract{title?, source?, fields:[{k, v?, g?, hot?, link?, delta?, revealAt?, hideAt?}], note?}Message-contract card: a compact "on the wire" field table. delta is added|removed|changed; reveal indices bind the row to this section's diagram steps. Optional source chip on the card title and footer note.
      
      
      diagram.view"ambient" | "step" | "ambient-only"How the board opens. ambient (default): live view with an AMBIENT/STEP toggle when steps exist. step: opens as the click-through at step 1. ambient-only: no toggle — for boards without a meaningful sequence. One diagram spec always drives both flavors.
      
      
      diagram.autoplaybooleanDefaults to false: step view opens paused. Set true to advance every 3 seconds when step view opens. Workbench and Confluence configuration previews stay paused; reduced motion disables automatic steps. No schema-version change needed.
      
      
      diagram.nodes{id: {title?, sub?, icon?, tint?, group?, link?}}Service cards. icon from the shared library (default gear); use Browse icons to search names or filter categories; tint colors the icon chip (default cmd). group: containment-boundary membership. link: optional permalink — a small clickable ↗ on the card corner, new tab.
      
      
      diagram.groups{groupId: {title?}}Declares containment boundaries: a dashed titled box drawn around all member nodes (a device holding two chips). Put members in one stack column; an edge between stack members draws as a vertical interconnect.
      
      
      diagram.rows[[slot, ...], ...]Slots render left to right in every row. A slot is a node id, or an array of ids = a stack (members render top to bottom in one column). Cross-row edges follow their endpoint positions.
      
      
      diagram.routing"curves" | "lanes"Optional lane routing reserves tracks and ports around cards. Supports 1–5 unstacked cards per row, no floats or self-loops; otherwise warns and uses curves. New diagrams, catalog seeds, trace imports and built-in template projects default to no lanes. Select the section heading, then Inspect → Edge routing to switch. Readable size enlarges the board for horizontal scrolling.
      
      
      diagram.floats[{id, side:"above", x?, y?}]Nodes outside the rows. Without coordinates, above/below placement is automatic. Both x and y pin the center in diagram units. Drag any float to pin it; use inspector Float X/Y for precision or choose Auto above/below to release it. Row nodes keep their row/slot gestures.
      
      
      diagram.edges{from, to, kind?, ret?, label?, fromPort?, toPort?, bend?, labelDx?, labelDy?, revealAt?, hideAt?}kind is the protocol (default int). Optional ports are {side:"top|right|bottom|left",offset:0.5}, with offset 0–1 along the side. Inspector Exit/Entry side and position (%) pin endpoints; Auto restores routing. Pinned edges use curves even in lane layouts. Zero-based reveal indices draw the edge only for the selected step interval; bend/label offsets tune geometry.
      
      
      diagram.layouts[{id,name,presentation?,sectionLayout,steps?,exploreLayout?}]Named views of one story. presentation:"standard" (default) uses the saved arrangement; "explore" uses a full-height graph, independent floating panels and pinned steps. Explore stays visible while editing. exploreLayout saves floating panel/control rectangles as viewport fractions and camera:{zoom,x,y} as scale and SVG-relative center; workbench gestures update these defaults with Undo. Presentation belongs to the view across host profiles. Arrange section → Presentation edits it in one Undo/Redo operation. defaultLayout picks the opening view ID. Layout guide.
      
      
      diagram.sectionLayout{default:[{x:0,y:0,w:8,h:12},{panel:"home",x:8,y:0,w:4,h:12}]}Saved twelve-column tile layouts: default, backstage, confluence. Use controls:"steps" for a movable playback/path/caption tile. Arrange section to drag/resize; Preview selects the target and Optimize layout supplies a starting arrangement. Coordinates are zero-based, height 3–40 rows. Unspecified tiles stay visible; narrow views stack. Layout guide.
      
      
      diagram.primaryPanel"home"Optional centerpiece panel ID: show it large with playback below it and a collapsible Data flow underneath. Set Presentation → Centerpiece in the panel inspector. Homemap steps have device states, subject drag/tap placement, visibility, inheritance, and signal controls.
      
      
      diagram.brand{app?, icon?, logo?, logoImage?, accent?, bg?, fg?}Shared company branding for Phone, Device app, Camera screen and Security monitoring. Select a panel, then open Company branding to edit shared settings, override this panel or hide its brand. panel.brand inherits when absent, suppresses with false, and overrides with a partial object. Choose a library icon, 1–4 character monogram, or upload an embedded PNG/JPEG/WebP up to 512 KiB. Colors use #RGB or #RRGGBB.
      
      
      diagram.panels[{id, type, title?, ...}]Synchronized inspector widgets beside the board. Panel types are documented in contract/authoring-contract.md, including static embedded image references, table for data snapshots, checks for authored decisions, budget for resource limits, and replicas for positions and reported lag. waterfall supports startMs offsets for overlapping trace spans; trace shows service internals and child-covered versus uncovered wall time.
      
      
      steps[n].id"ota.3"Optional unique step identifier for deep links, search and preview restoration. Duplicating a step gives its copy a new ID.
      
      
      diagram.paths[{id, label?, color?, steps:[step IDs]}]Optional named outcomes sharing one step registry and board. First path is the default. Chips start paths at step 1. Shared beginnings use clickable shadows; consecutive shared IDs after divergence form a common track. Paths can split and rejoin again. Shared ending means all participating paths finish there; early endings never connect to later blocks they do not visit. Full authored sequences determine blocks, including hidden stops. Numbers, playback and state follow the selected participating path. Shared circles keep it when possible and identify the participating path otherwise. Conflicting shared orders retain separate occurrences with sharing cues. No path label unless alternates exist. Story steps can fork, rename, recolor and remove paths.
      
      
      diagram.steps[{edge | edges, nodes?, panels?, lane?, text, link?}]Ordered narrative. edge:"from->to" or edges:[...] for hops that happen together — their packets fire in order, staggered. A step may be edgeless: light nodes:[...] directly and/or patch panels. panels carries SPARSE per-panel patches; the engine folds them into complete per-step state so any jump is consistent (log appends; enterOnce applies only at its own step). Drives the numbered coins, the ambient packet schedule, AND the click-through.
      
      
      step.failures{"from->to":"dropped" | "blocked"}Current-step communication outcomes. Dropped packets stop at an orange break and fade; blocked communications show a stop marker without sending. Failed hops override normal packets and focus only their source unless nodes explicitly select the destination. Static markers remain with reduced motion. Edit with each hop’s Delivery selector or Add failed communication.
      
      
      iconsUse Browse icons for the shared library across nodes, groups, Home elements, Device app cards and company marks. Categories include Power, Temperature, Security, Connectivity, Audio and Dispatch; examples: battery-full battery-low battery-charging hot cold armed disarmed triggered camera wifi headset. Icon IDs and recipe.
      
      
      tintscmd auth data mqtt dev
      
      
      scenesperson-at-door-night person-through-door doorbell-run-away doorbell-runners package-drop kitchen-fire static-noise (stock scenes for the screen widget)
      
    
      
    
      

    
      Reserved fields (forward-compatible, not yet rendered)
      
    
      Shaped now so richer renderers can add them without
    breaking existing specs. Today's engine tolerates and ignores them.

      steps[n].stickytrue | falseExplicit persistence flag for board effects across steps (panel state already persists via patch folding).
      
    
      
    
      

    
      
      
      Handles well
        
        
          
      • Tabbed multi-section pages from one JSON — diagrams and click-throughs side by side
        • 
          
      • One diagram spec, both flavors: ambient + step playback from the same steps
        • 
          
      • Synchronized inspector panels: state machines, LEDs, gauges, logs, camera screen — sparse patches folded to complete per-step state
        • 
          
      • Containment groups (a device boundary around chips) with vertical stack interconnects
        • 
          
      • Left-to-right rows with 3–5 slots; stacks of 2–4; automatic or freely positioned floats
        • 
          
      • Legend, edges, packets, and arrowheads all from the one protocol table
        • 
        
      
      
      
      
      Known limits (by design, for now)
        
        
          
      • Automatic avoidance is best-effort; crowded corridors may need ports, bend or label nudges
        • 
          
      • Hidden tabs stop painting, but SMIL clocks keep running — ambient dots are mid-path when a tab is revealed (harmless for loops)
        • 
          
      • Switching tabs pauses a click-through. In this workbench, use Play to resume from the same step.
        • 
          
      • Freely placed nodes can overlap; choose their positions and check the resulting connections
        • 
          
      • Group members must be placed adjacently (one stack column works best); the boundary is a bounding box, not a layout constraint
        •
